methods.description: Name the complete group of interest and decide whether data come from every member (census) or only part (sample); explain definitions, misleading size/collector arguments and the same collection relative to different populations using that criterion.

Choose census or sample from the stated information required and practical time/cost: collect from everyone when every individual result is needed or the small group is manageable; use part when whole-group collection is impractical. Do not guarantee error-free measurements.
Explain that a test uses up an item or leaves it unfit for sale, so testing only part of the population leaves remaining stock available; testing every item is possible but unsuitable for sale stock.

sourceReview.locator: Stage 4 Data analysis: complete census/sample definitions and data-collection conclusion dot points
sourceReview.observation: Defines census as every unit in the population and sample as a subset selected to represent the population of interest. These are data-collection concepts, not probability sample spaces.
sourceReview.adjustments: Earliest governing Stage 4 context retained. No probability outcomes, advanced sampling classifications, parameters or numerical inference methods are imported.

sourceReview.locator: Surveys: complete definitions, original population/collection identification teaching and complete ten-part practice question
sourceReview.observation: Original definitions name the population as every individual of interest, census as whole population and sample as part. Source scenarios include adults, whales, Sydney residents, voters, factory pens, river water, household votes, automatic counting, schools and workplace/store surveys. Actually viewed original image188: twelve penguins in the defined whole group and four selected penguins pictured as the sample.
sourceReview.adjustments: Rejected automatic Probability Outcomes and Sample Space selection as the wrong meaning of sample; prepared original evidence remains immutable. Adapted the original collection scenarios to four concise population-relative examples. The original classification scaffold says Census|Survey although both are surveys; student-facing classifications consistently say census or sample. Cost/time, individual costume measurements and destructive stock tests are simple applications of the whole/part definition to the stated situation, not falsely attributed to filled source worked examples. Repaired census-guarantees-exactness and literal jar-destruction/census-impossibility overclaims without introducing a sampling-bias lesson.
